title: The media-service integration suite referenced the non-existent Docker image 'minio/minio:latest' - 44 integration tests could never run, anywhere
actual: AbstractMediaIntegrationTest declared new MinIOContainer(DockerImageName.parse("minio/minio:latest")). That tag no longer exists on Docker Hub: 'docker pull minio/minio:latest' and 'docker pull minio/minio:RELEASE.2024-09-13T20-26-02Z' both return 'pull access denied for minio/minio, repository does not exist or may require docker login'. The container start therefore failed in the static initializer with ContainerFetchException -> ExceptionInInitializerError -> NoClassDefFoundError for every media integration test class (UploadIT 13, MediaOutboxIT 10, MediaOutboxClaimConcurrencyIT 2, MediaOutboxRetentionIT 3, MediaPurgeIT 4, ProvisioningIT 4 and others - 44 errors in total). The suite also used a DIFFERENT S3 implementation from production, which deploys RustFS.
expected: Integration tests must be runnable in CI and locally, and the object-storage test double should be the implementation the platform actually ships against.
trigger: Any execution of the media-service integration suite.
root_cause: An unpinned and now-deleted upstream image tag, plus a fidelity gap between the test double (MinIO) and production (RustFS).
consequences: 44 integration tests were permanently unrunnable and therefore silently unverified: upload, WebP processing, presigned URLs, outbox relay/retention/claim concurrency, purge job and bucket provisioning for the media domain. A green 'mvn test' in CI would have been impossible for media-service, and the media domain's correctness claims had no executable evidence.
remediation: Replace the MinIO container with the production RustFS image (rustfs/rustfs:1.0.0-rc.5) and the same credential environment the compose stack uses (RUSTFS_ACCESS_KEY / RUSTFS_SECRET_KEY), with a readiness wait on the S3 health endpoint. This both unblocks the suite and raises fidelity to the shipped backend.
regression_test: The media-service module suite itself is the regression evidence: 126 tests, 0 failures after the change (44 errors before).
remediation_applied: AbstractMediaIntegrationTest now boots rustfs/rustfs:1.0.0-rc.5 with RUSTFS_VOLUMES/RUSTFS_ADDRESS/RUSTFS_CONSOLE_ADDRESS/RUSTFS_CONSOLE_ENABLE/RUSTFS_ACCESS_KEY/RUSTFS_SECRET_KEY, waits on /minio/health/live, and publishes the endpoint through shop.storage.endpoint.
verification_evidence: media-service module: 126 tests, 0 failures, 0 errors (previously 44 errors).

title: Shared Testcontainers databases are polluted across test classes, making several integration tests order-dependent
actual: Each service boots ONE PostgreSQL/Kafka container per JVM and every integration test class in the module shares it. Several tests assume an empty table or a stable row ordering. Observed failures: InventoryOutboxClaimConcurrencyTest failed with 'Expecting actual: Optional[2] to contain: 3L' because a background @Scheduled job from another cached ApplicationContext inserted an outbox row between the test's purge and its claim; PromotionBootstrapIT failed with 'expected: 0L but was: 16L' because another test class had created 16 campaigns; NotificationFlowIT asserted a terminal row status immediately after the row appeared (the row is inserted PENDING and updated later), which is a race; auth-service logged 'duplicate key value violates unique constraint users_username_key' from a repeated username.
expected: Every integration test must be deterministic regardless of the order in which the module's test classes run.
trigger: Running the whole module's suite (the tests pass individually).
root_cause: A shared container plus several cached ApplicationContexts, each with its own @Scheduled tasks, all mutating the same database while other test classes are asserting on it; plus tests that assert on non-final state without waiting for it.
consequences: The suite is order-dependent and flaky. Two of the failures were masked entirely by the timezone defect (F-039): the integration contexts could not boot, so the polluting code never ran. Fixing the timezone exposed them - a good illustration that a defect can hide the evidence of another.
remediation: inventory: disable the background relay and the reservation-cleanup sweep by default in the IT base and delay the sweep's first run; promotion: truncate the campaign tables before asserting an empty table; notification: wait for the terminal row status instead of the row's existence.
regression_test: The module suites themselves - inventory-service 64 tests, promotion-service 120 tests, notification-service 94 tests, all green and order-independent.
remediation_applied: inventory AbstractIntegrationTest pins inventory.outbox.poll-interval-ms and inventory.reservation-cleanup-*-ms to 1h; ReservationCleanupScheduler gained an initialDelayString; promotion PromotionBootstrapIT truncates before asserting; notification NotificationFlowIT gained awaitRowWithStatus.
